Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-29
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Samira Lopez (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (Glasswing CTO), Rajiv Menon (Glasswing Head of ML), Evelyn Hart (Glasswing Platform Eng), Noah Greene (Glasswing Security)

Auto-summary (auto):

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Appreciate you fitting this in. Quick intro from Redwood side — I'm Maya, AE, and Owen and Samira are our SEs. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Lina (CTO): Hi, thanks. Doing well. We grabbed an hour. We've been kicking the tires on a couple of APIs, want to understand the fastest way to get first tokens and then what it looks like to move to dedicated or private.
[00:18] Owen (SE): Great. We'll cover quickstart credits, TTFT — time to first token — and then sketch out dedicated/reserved and VPC/private paths. Quick note, apologies if audio drops, my mic is new.
[00:28] Rajiv (Head ML): No problem. Quick context: our product is a contextual search + doc assistant embedded in our app. Typical requests are 1.5k–4k tokens per session, and we expect bursty traffic up to ~350 qps peak during business hours. Latency is critical — p50 under 150ms ideally for generation tail.
[00:45] Samira (SE): Thanks Rajiv. Couple clarifying q's — is most of your data user-generated PII, and do you need on-prem?
[00:52] Rajiv: Mostly user-generated; some PII but we can tokenise. Regulation-wise, we need strong audit logs and KMS for key control. We are exploring hosted first to iterate fast; if we see predictable throughput needs we might want dedicated GPUs or even private VPC deployment.
[01:04] Maya: Perfect — that's the sweet spot Redwood targets. We have PLG credits for quickstart so you can get to first request in hours. From there customers often either stay on Hosted API for speed to market or move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale, and Private/VPC when they need network isolation and customer-managed keys.
[01:20] Lina: Can you explain the difference in terms of SLAs and cost? We want to know when to switch.
[01:26] Owen: Sure. Hosted is pay-as-you-go, per-token pricing and embeddings, and we give free first-credit package to run proofs. No cold-start reserved capacity so latency can vary although we optimize routing and have prefix caching. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools — you get throughput SLOs and consistent latency since capacity is owned; pricing is committed monthly. Private adds the private control plane/VPC and KMS integration for full key control and audit log retention.
[01:45] Rajiv: How big a delta is latency between hosted and dedicated?
[01:48] Samira: In our benchmarks internal we see hosted p50 around 140–220ms depending on model/sequence length; dedicated can be tuned lower and gives more predictable p95 because there is less noisy neighbor effect. For high qps you also get better batching control on Dedicated. Note: our transcriptions call it "Redwood Dedicate" sometimes, sorry for the slip.
[02:04] Noah (Security): On KMS — do you integrate with customer AWS KMS / GCP KMS and HSM? Need to know for compliance.
[02:10] Owen: Yes we support KMS integrations for Private deployments and for Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via KMS in the VPC setup; hosted can integrate for at-rest envelope keys, but HSM-level hardware key custody is part of our Private offering (or via partner HSM for Dedicated in some cases). We'll send the KMS diagram in the doc pack.
[02:25] Lina: Audit logs and retention — we need 12 months of audit logs for model calls and administrative actions.
[02:31] Maya: That's common. We have audit log exports and can retain logs per contract. We'll include retention options and whether logs are stored in the cloud or delivered to your S3.
[02:40] Rajiv: Ok, about TTFT — what's realistic? We want devs to prototype in hours and get a small pilot in production in 2–4 weeks.
[02:48] Maya: With free credits and our quickstart templates you can be calling the API in a few hours. Time-to-first-token for a basic integration is often under 1–2 hours if you use the SDKs and follow our guides. For a pilot with canary traffic, 2–4 weeks is a realistic runway if you handle the application integration and data privacy checks quickly.
[03:03] Samira: For the hosted benchmark, we can provision you credits, run a scripted load with your sample payloads, and show p50/p95/p99 latency and token cost. That helps you decide dedicated vs hosted.
[03:15] Evelyn (Platform): That sounds useful. We need the benchmark to use our real prompts and document shards, because we see heavy KV cache reuse in production — do you support prefix/KV caching in hosted?
[03:25] Owen: Yes — both Hosted and Dedicated support KV cache behavior and prefix caching. On Hosted we have automatic prefix caching heuristics; on Dedicated you can tune cache sizing and eviction policies more directly.
[03:36] Rajiv: If we hit sustained 350 qps, what's the ops difference between spinning up Dedicated vs bursting on Hosted?
[03:42] Maya: Hosted can handle bursts but cost and tail-latency can spike during extreme loads. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput for a commit. We can recommend autoscale and burst policies; committed reserved capacity is priced to be cheaper per-token if you have predictable usage.
[03:55] Lina: Any enterprise features around RBAC and SSO? We use Okta; need role separation for devs vs ops.
[04:01] Owen: Yes SSO via SAML/Okta is supported, as is fine-grained RBAC in the console. For Private we can map to your AD through LDAP. We'll include a quick security matrix in the docs.
[04:12] Noah: What about data residency — can you keep inference in eu-west-1 only?
[04:16] Samira: Yes, Hosted supports regional routing; for strict residency Dedicated or Private is the usual path because you can pin capacity to a region and apply network egress controls. We'll clarify which models are available in which regions — some open models have region-specific performance profiles.
[04:30] Rajiv: Budget question — how much do you expect for a pilot? Rough numbers suffice.
[04:34] Maya: For a small hosted benchmark and a 2-week pilot using hosted credits, typically a few thousand dollars of credits covers evaluation. Dedicated pilots vary — but if you want a reserved node for a month that's an order higher; we'll put numbers in the spreadsheet. We'll share an example cost sheet with per-token vs reserved monthly math.
[04:51] Lina: Do you provide tooling for rollout/rollback and canarying?
[04:55] Owen: Yes — Redwood console has rollout features, canary lanes, model pinning, and automatic fallback policies. It's the same console across Hosted/Dedicated/Private so your devs use the same workflow.
[05:06] Rajiv: For the benchmark, we care about generation tokenization and cost visibility — need token-level cost per route/model.
[05:12] Samira: We can provide token-level cost breakdowns per model and route. We'll append a sample per-route report from an internal run.
[05:20] Lina: Anything about model compatibility — are there model constraints that change in Private? We use some quantized variants.
[05:25] Owen: Private supports the same model catalog; it also allows custom model onboarding subject to compatibility checks. Some extremely quantized kernels may require specific runtime flags; we'll list recommended quantization profiles per model for Private and Dedicated.
[05:37] Rajiv: From a timeline POV if we do hosted benchmark next week and it looks good, can we start a Dedicated evaluation in July?
[05:44] Maya: Yes, that's doable. Typical flow: hosted quickstart + benchmark -> 2-week pilot -> decide Dedicated pilot or Private scoping. We'll schedule the Dedicated scoping once benchmark results are in.
[05:55] Evelyn: On the sample data we'll share: a small set of doc shards and a replay of 24 hours of traffic to simulate burstiness. Will that be enough?
[06:03] Samira: That's perfect. The replay helps us measure KV cache hit rates and realistic batching. Please obfuscate PII in the samples.
[06:11] Noah: Any legal or procurement blockers we should expect? Contractual SLAs, data processing addenda?
[06:16] Maya: For Hosted we have standard DPA and terms; for Dedicated/Private there are enterprise agreements and SOWs covering SLA/retention. We'll surface the DPA and our standard security annex.
[06:28] Rajiv: Cool. On benchmarks — will you run them or do we run them?
[06:32] Owen: We can run an initial hosted benchmark with your samples (we'll use a controlled runner), or we can provide the script for you to run in your environment. Many customers prefer we run the first pass and share results.
[06:44] Lina: Perfect. I have a question about caching semantics — if we run many short sessions with overlapping histories, do you have prefix similarity caching?
[06:51] Samira: Yes, our caching layer attempts prefix dedupe and key-value cache reuse. It reduces cost by avoiding re-computation when the KV cache is warm; again, Dedicated gives you more control over cache sizing and eviction.
[07:04] Rajiv: Alright, last bit — any hidden costs for streaming/long-context models?
[07:09] Maya: Streaming is supported; long-context models have higher token cost and memory footprint. We'll include cost per-TB memory usage and guidance on quantized models that reduce memory and cost.
[07:21] Lina: Ok, let's recap.
[07:24] Maya: Recap: Redwood will send SOC2 and security docs, KMS integration diagram, and a cost spreadsheet. We'll provision quickstart credits for Glasswing and propose a hosted benchmark plan. Glasswing will share sample payloads, qps shape and a 24-hour traffic replay. We'll aim to run a hosted benchmark week of 2026-07-06. After results we schedule a Dedicated scoping call.
[07:45] Rajiv: That matches. One more thing — can we get a named contact for engineering during the benchmark?
[07:49] Owen: Yes, that will be me and Samira. We'll include contact details in the follow-up.
[07:55] Lina: Great, thanks everyone.
[07:57] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.
